Fix ICE-over-TCP receive path teardown and end of stream recursion (#1771)

Two ways the ICE-over-TCP receive path could be lost, one of which takes the
whole process with it.

1. Malformed TURN data indication (GHSA-mwf8-6m4x-pgmm)

A TURN data indication with no DATA attribute, or with a zero length one,
leaves the relayed payload null once it is extracted in OnRTPPacketReceived.
The length guard in that handler is applied to the original data indication,
before the payload is extracted, so the discriminator byte reads after it
dereferenced the null payload and threw.

On the UDP receive path the base UdpReceiver logs and drops such a packet, so
the throw is contained. IceTcpReceiver overrides EndReceiveFrom and had kept
the catch-all that calls Close(), which the base class dropped when the same
anti-pattern was fixed previously. Close() sets m_isClosed, which makes the
re-arm in the finally block a no-op and also permanently disables the re-arm
in RtpIceChannel.SendOverTCP, so a single malformed packet left the
ICE-over-TCP receive path dead for the rest of the session. Where a plaintext
TURN-over-TCP relay is the only viable media path (UDP blocked by a
restrictive NAT or fire

Validate SCTP SACK gap ack block and duplicate TSN counts (#1772)

SctpSackChunk.ParseChunk read the gap ack block and duplicate TSN counts
straight from the chunk and looped that many times, four bytes per iteration,
without checking either count against the length the chunk declared. Both are
supplied by the remote party and each allows up to 65535 entries, while
NetConvert.ParseUInt16/32 index the buffer without bounds checks of their own.

With the maximum count the gap ack loop reaches offset 262144 in the 262144
byte receive buffer on the 65529th iteration and throws
IndexOutOfRangeException. That is a SystemException, so the recoverable
catch (ApplicationException) in RTCSctpTransport.DoReceive is skipped and the
generic handler breaks out of the receive loop. The receive thread is created
and started once with no restart, so a single crafted SACK chunk from a
negotiated peer left the association and every data channel permanently dead.

Below the buffer size there is no exception at all. The receive buffer is
allocated once and reused, so a chunk declaring length 16 with a count of, say,

Mark TurnServer experimental with diagnostic SIPSORCERY001 (#1773)

TurnServer is written for development, testing and small scale or embedded
scenarios, not for production. The XML documentation says so and lists the
limitations in detail, but a doc comment is easy to miss and carries no weight
at build time, so package consumers have had no real signal.

ExperimentalAttribute is the purpose built mechanism for this. Referencing
TurnServer is now a compile error until SIPSORCERY001 is suppressed, which
makes using it a deliberate decision rather than something discovered after
deployment. UrlFormat points the diagnostic at docs/diagnostics/SIPSORCERY001.md,
which spells out what is missing: no nonce validation or expiry, no rate
limiting or per-IP allocation caps, no TLS/DTLS on the control channel,
uncapped allocation lifetimes, UDP only relay, IPv4 only.

The attribute comes from the Polyfill package already referenced, so it applies
across all nine target frameworks including net462 and netstandard2.0 with no
project changes.

Obsolete was considered and rejected: it is only a warning, it renders with
strikethrough implying imminent removal, and TurnServer is not deprecated.
Ed

Detect a half closed ICE server TCP connection instead of sending into it (#1776)

Socket.Connected reports the state as of the last I/O operation and stays true
after the remote end closes the connection gracefully, so SendOverTCP could not
tell a half closed connection from a live one. It sent into the dead connection
and the ICE server check retried until the request count or timeout heuristics
happened to give up.

IceTcpReceiver already detects the close for real, since a zero byte receive on
a stream socket is the end of stream. That is now surfaced as IsEndOfStream and
SendOverTCP checks it before sending, returning SocketError.NotConnected. The
caller records that against the ICE server, which takes it out of the running
and lets the checklist move to the next one, so the failure is deterministic and
immediate rather than incidental.

No reconnect is attempted, because there is no way to do one in place. A
connected socket cannot be reused: Socket.Connect throws
InvalidOperationException after Socket.Disconnect, and not only for the same
endpoint as the exception message suggests but for any endpoint, with
reuseSocket true. That is measured, and pinned by a test so a future

Update the bundled Twig fork to the current 3.x

Relocks twig/twig from 24d7a0e (3.26.0 base) to 5404489, which merges 181
upstream commits including the 3.27 and 3.28 releases.

The fork's Grav patches survive the sync. Upstream 3.27 replaced
Parser::filterBodyNodes() with cleanupBodyForChildTemplates() plus the new
CorrectnessNodeVisitor, so the "block definition under an if" support was
re-homed across both: the visitor keeps IfNode off its tag stack, and the
parser strips the block reference underneath so a conditional block override
is registered without also rendering in place.

No new CVEs in this range; the 2025-2026 sandbox and XSS fixes were already
in the 3.26 base shipped with 2.0.19.

Verified with the unit suite and by rendering the front end, forum and admin
of a full site.

Make the Twig integration compatible with Twig 3.28+

The bundled Twig fork is being synced from 3.26 to the current 3.x, which brings
in two signature changes Grav builds on:

* EscaperExtension::setEscaper() gained a "void" return type. The anonymous
  subclass in TwigEnvironment that shims setEscaper() onto EscaperRuntime kept
  the old signature, which is a hard fatal on every request.
* SecurityPolicyInterface::checkSecurity() gained a fourth "$tests" argument,
  deprecated to omit since 3.28 and required from Twig 4.0.

GravSecurityPolicy takes the argument and an optional $allowedTests list. That
list defaults to null, leaving tests unrestricted exactly as the sandbox
behaved before 3.28; wiring it to security.yaml is a separate decision.

Both changes are compatible with the currently pinned 3.26, so this can land
ahead of the Twig bump.

Stop a subfolder .htaccess from disabling the root security rules

mod_rewrite rules are not inherited by subdirectories. An .htaccess in a
theme or plugin folder that turns on RewriteEngine replaces the root
ruleset for that folder and everything beneath it, so a package shipping
its own .htaccess to block one file silently exposed its .yaml, .md,
.twig and .php files. Adding `RewriteOptions Inherit` only half fixes it:
the root rules anchored on a path (`^(user)/...`) still cannot match,
because a per-directory rewrite strips the directory prefix first.

Require/FilesMatch access control is merged into subdirectories rather
than replaced, so a user/.htaccess written that way holds regardless of
what a subfolder does with rewriting. It denies the same extensions the
root rule blocks, plus dot-files. Files inside a dot-directory still
depend on the rewrite rules, since DirectoryMatch is not allowed in
.htaccess.

user/ and .htaccess are both in the installer $ignores list, so existing
installs get the file from a postflight instead, following the pattern of
the 2026-06-09 heal. Sites that already have their own user/.htaccess are
left alone.

Fixes #4236

Ship the Twig sandbox defaults in code and restore Twig-in-content by default

Move the ~300-line Twig sandbox allowlists out of security.yaml into
Grav\Common\Twig\Sandbox\SandboxDefaults. The allowed_* config keys are now
additive over these defaults rather than replacing them, so a site's overrides
can no longer freeze the shipped baseline against later security tightenings.
Add denied_* keys to tighten below the defaults, plus an installer migration
(logic in the unit-tested Security::planSandboxDefaultsMigration) that converts
a site's previously-tightened allowlists into explicit denied_*, preserving the
exact effective policy across the upgrade.

Flip security.twig_content.process_enabled to true so page-content Twig renders
on new installs. Remove the option/select entries from xss_dangerous_tags, whose
stored-XSS sink is fixed at source in the form plugin and whose real payload is
still caught by on_events. Drop the twig_sandbox.logging and admin_hint toggles;
both behaviours are now always on. Add Security::describeEffectiveSandbox() to
back the admin effective-policy view.

Signed-off-by: Andy Miller <rhuk@mac.com>

[security] Scan modular page content for XSS at save time The save-time guard against render-time-assembled XSS in page content (Security::detectXssInEditorContent, added for GHSA-2c4f-86xc-cr74) and the render-time sinks computed different booleans for "will Twig run over this body?": render: ($gate && $page->shouldProcess('twig')) || $page->isModule() save: $gate && $page->shouldProcess('twig') <- no modular branch security.twig_content.process_enabled ships false, so a modular page executed its body Twig at render while the save-time scan was skipped entirely. Turning the gate on did not help either: a module rarely sets process.twig, so shouldProcess('twig') was false and the guard bailed out regardless. There was no configuration in which modular content was scanned. An account with only page-edit rights could therefore store a Twig-assembled payload -- `{% autoescape false %}{{ "" }}` -- that the raw-source validator cannot see, and it rendered live for every visitor to the page embedding the module wherever the theme's modular template emits `{{ content|raw }}`. Extract the decision into Security::willProcessContentTwig()

fix(data-apps): block re-entry into handleSubmit during image upload (#22612)

The image-upload + clarify awaits in `handleSubmit` opened a multi-second
window where `isLoading` was still false (no mutation had started), so
spamming Enter or the send button kicked off duplicate iterations against
the same app. The backend's "version already building" guard rejected the
losers as 400s, surfacing as a flurry of "Failed to generate app" rows
even though one iteration succeeded in the background.

Add a synchronous `isSubmittingRef` guard at the top of `handleSubmit`
plus an `isSubmitting` state for UI lock-out, released in a `finally`.
While the upload is in flight, the image chip shows a `LoadingOverlay`
in place of its remove button and the resource sections forward a
`disabled` prop so charts/dashboard chips can't be yanked mid-flight.
The "Generating your app" placeholder bubble is gated on a new
`isAgentWorking` derivation so it doesn't appear before the prompt has
actually been sent.

feat: load AWS extension for DuckDB credential chain when static S3 credentials are absent (#22606)

Closes:

### Description:

When using DuckDB with S3 credential chain (i.e. no static access/secret keys configured, relying on IRSA/web identity tokens or other SDK-based credential resolution), the `aws` DuckDB extension is now automatically installed and loaded before executing queries. This ensures that credential chain-based authentication works correctly in both regular query sessions and pre-aggregate sessions.

The `usesS3CredentialChain` helper was introduced to centralize the logic for determining whether static credentials are absent, replacing the inline boolean check in `buildS3SecretSql` and reusing it to conditionally load the `aws` extension. Tests were added to verify that `INSTALL aws;` and `LOAD aws;` are called when using credential chain auth, and are not called when static credentials are provided.

Parse the judge verdict even when wrapped in prose

Some judge models (e.g. gemma2) ignore "respond ONLY with JSON" and append
chatty text after the verdict object. json.loads on the whole string then fails,
and the keyword fallback saw both "yes" and "no" (the trailing "Let me know"
contains "no" inside "know"), so a correct "yes" was scored as a fail. Parse
the first JSON object with raw_decode and ignore any surrounding prose.

Drop interrupted-response stragglers in the eval harness

When a user barges in, the interrupted response can still flush one last LLM
token *after* the bot-interrupted event (it was generated before the interrupt
propagated). The harness aggregated that straggler as the new turn's reply and
the judge failed it before the real answer arrived (e.g. an interruption turn saw
'what would' from the abandoned story instead of 'The capital of Japan is
Tokyo.'). Suppress llm_response segments after an interruption until the next
bot-llm-started, which marks the genuinely new response.

Rename EvalVoice to EvalSpeech

The scenario config block is `user: speech:`, and the sibling helpers already
track their config keys (`transcription:` -> EvalTranscriber). Rename the class
(and voice.py -> speech.py, the `voice`/`_voice` params and attributes, and the
`voice` log category) to EvalSpeech so it matches `speech:`. The TTS voice id
(`voice_cfg`, the `voice` setting) is unchanged.

Generate eval user audio via run_tts instead of a pipeline

EvalSpeech spun up a whole PipelineWorker + WorkerRunner + AsyncGeneratorProcessor
(plus an identity serializer) just to synthesize one utterance. Replace that with
a minimal frame-processor lifecycle: give the TTS service a task manager, a clock,
and a StartFrame, then call run_tts() directly and collect the audio frames.

Restrict to local or HTTP services (the built-ins, Kokoro and CartesiaHttp,
already are) and reject websocket-streaming TTS with a clear error -- run_tts
can't be driven without a pipeline to manage its connection. enable_metrics is
off so run_tts never tries to push a MetricsFrame with no downstream.

Deliver eval user audio gap-free to avoid split turns

The mic sender streamed one ~20ms frame per 20ms tick, including the user's
speech. The suite runs several sessions on one event loop, which under load can
slip a tick by hundreds of ms; a gap that lands mid-utterance makes a
turn-detecting STT (e.g. Deepgram Flux) finalize early, splitting "what is two
plus two" into "what is two" + "plus two" so the bot answers the wrong
question. The audio samples are contiguous, so drain queued user audio promptly
(ahead of real time) instead of one frame per tick -- the whole utterance reaches
the bot gap-free regardless of loop stalls. Silence is still paced in real time
so the bot's VAD ends each turn.

Record the speech/transcription/judge config in the eval log

The terminal summary shows which services and models a run used, but the saved
eval.log did not, so diagnosing a flake meant cross-referencing config (e.g.
which Whisper model produced a bad transcription). Write the describe_config
summary into the eval.log too, and include the transcription model and TTS voice
in that summary (previously only the service name was shown).

Run the eval bot-speech transcriber on the CPU

Whisper defaulted to device=auto, putting the transcriber on the GPU alongside
the judge -- so transcription model size and concurrency were both bounded by GPU
memory. Bot-speech transcription runs once per turn off the hot path, so move it
to the CPU (device=cpu, int8) by default. The GPU then holds only the judge
(~8.5GB peak, constant in concurrency), freeing room for a larger, more accurate
transcriber (distil-medium or large-v3-turbo) at higher concurrency on a 16GB
GPU. device/compute_type are overridable via the transcription config.

Cap per-model CPU threads so concurrent transcriptions share cores

Scenarios start in lockstep with the same greeting+first-turn duration, so on CPU
their first Whisper transcriptions fire at once. Uncapped, CTranslate2 grabs ~all
cores per model, so N models oversubscribe the CPU N-fold -- the first turn crawls
and only speeds up once the runs drift out of sync (exactly the staggered-finish
behavior observed). Cap each model to cores/concurrency OpenMP threads via
OMP_NUM_THREADS (CT2 honors it; verified ~3.7x between 1 and 12 threads), so total
threads stay ~= cores on every turn -- no oversubscription, no staggering. Respects
an explicit OMP_NUM_THREADS override.
